I have been farming these 6 mu for 30 years, and wheat-maize rotation is what works on our soil here in Quzhou. I finished high school so I read the fertilizer bags and I listen to what the agriculture station says, but I still trust what my own field has shown me over the years.

For wheat this winter season, I will plant an improved variety — Jimai or something similar that my neighbors had good results with last year. I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, about 50 kg per mu before sowing, that gives me roughly 7.5 kg each of N, P, and K. Then I top-dress with urea at jointing stage, about 20 kg per mu, which adds another 9 kg of nitrogen. So total nitrogen comes to around 16-17 kg per mu. I irrigate 3 times from the well — once after sowing if the soil is dry, once at jointing with the top-dress, once at grain filling. That is enough water if the spring rain is normal. I spray 2 times, once for aphids and once for rust or powdery mildew if I see it. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For summer maize after wheat harvest, I use hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335 type. No-till direct seeding into the wheat stubble saves me labor and moisture. Base fertilizer 40 kg of compound at sowing, then top-dress urea 25 kg at the big trumpet stage. That gives me about 20 kg N total, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. I irrigate 2 times — once at sowing if dry, once at tasseling. Maize here needs pesticide for corn borer and armyworm, I spray 2 times. Expected yield around 600 kg per mu.

Every yuan counts on 6 mu, but I would rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than watch my yield drop. That has been my rule for 30 years.
